requirements.title: First-year preparation
requirements.summary: Four years of English, three of social studies, four of mathematics including algebra, geometry, trigonometry and precalculus; calculus preferred. Two to three years of science including chemistry or physics, both preferred. Computing is preferred.

requirements.title: Transfer preparation
requirements.summary: At least precalculus and chemistry or physics; computing courses are preferred. Internal transfers are accepted; students beyond the first two years should consult an advisor about remaining time.

requirements.title: Undergraduate transfer approval
requirements.summary: Transfer courses require institutional approval and a C or better. Previously evaluated credit applies only where it fits the chosen program. Enrolled degree students need prior written approval from the home dean/director or designee for outside coursework; applicable residency limits still apply.

requirements.title: Minor/major grading and noncredit limits
requirements.summary: Elected Pass/No Pass is limited to open electives and cannot satisfy a major, minor, general education or immersion requirement. X grades carry earned credit but no GPA or residency credit; audit and failed courses do not satisfy undergraduate residency. S-graded study abroad may carry residency and earned credit but no GPA; other undergraduate S categories do not carry credit or residency.

requirements.title: Repeated undergraduate courses
requirements.summary: The last grade earned in a repeated undergraduate course is final, even when lower. Outside courses and examination/experience credit cannot repeat prior coursework. Repeated or excluded coursework is annotated and excluded from the applicable prior GPA calculation.

requirements.title: Applicable undergraduate catalog
requirements.summary: Requirements normally follow the bulletin at program matriculation; a later advantageous bulletin may be chosen. The graduation bulletin cannot be more than seven calendar years old. Discontinued courses are not guaranteed; individual adjustments require the primary department head’s approval.

requirements.title: University graduation requirements
requirements.summary: Complete all required university and college courses, including applicable cooperative work; record all grades and resolve incompletes. A cumulative GPA of at least 2.00 is required.

requirements.title: Baccalaureate residency
requirements.summary: At least 25 percent of the degree’s total semester credit hours must be successfully completed RIT courses. The degree-granting program decides which specific courses qualify.

requirements.title: University baccalaureate minimum
requirements.summary: A baccalaureate degree requires at least 120 credit hours or the higher college/program total. This university floor does not replace the AI program’s published total.

requirements.title: Wellness, writing and administrative completion
requirements.summary: Complete the published wellness requirements and university writing competency requirements (D01.5). Financial obligations must be paid or satisfactorily adjusted; degree candidates are expected to attend commencement. The detailed D01.5 writing structure is represented separately.

requirements.title: Three writing-intensive courses
requirements.summary: Complete three credit-bearing writing-intensive courses within the degree: first-year FYW Writing Seminar or a designated three-credit FYW alternative approved by its director; a WI-PR course or sequence in the degree program; and a third WI course, ideally general education but permitted to be another WI-PR. Recommended year spacing is not a mandatory semester order. Exact AI-program WI designations still need verification.

requirements.title: BS general education distribution
requirements.summary: The BS general-education framework totals at least 60 semester hours: three First-Year Writing, 24 Perspectives, nine Immersion and remaining general-education electives (the framework table shows 24). These hours are part of the published degree total, not 60 additional hours.

requirements.title: Eight perspective courses across seven categories
requirements.summary: Complete one course in each of Ethical, Artistic, Global, Social, Natural Science Inquiry and Scientific Principles, plus two Mathematical Perspective courses. These eight courses fulfill the perspective distribution; program-designated courses can cover existing slots. A BS program may prescribe specific courses in no more than three perspective categories.

requirements.title: Primary-discipline general education limit
requirements.summary: At most three required courses, excluding laboratories, from the program’s primary discipline may count toward general education, and they must have approved General Education designation. Do not assume that every AI/computing course qualifies.

requirements.title: Immersion declaration and no program overlap
requirements.summary: Complete and declare an approved immersion of at least three related general-education courses totaling at least nine credits. Immersion courses may complement the major but cannot overlap program requirements. Programs cannot require one particular immersion or restrict the immersion group. A minor is optional and does not automatically satisfy an immersion.

requirements.title: Approved first-year writing alternatives
requirements.summary: The current university page lists UWRT-150 FYW: Writing Seminar and ISTE-110 FYW: Ethics in Computing as approved first-year writing courses. Other designated three-credit FYW alternatives require the program director’s approval. This general permission does not silently replace a more specific degree-course requirement.

requirements.title: Wellness exemptions, transfer and experiential credit
requirements.summary: The two required wellness activities must differ in activity or level. Exemptions cover age 25 or older at matriculation, six months of active military service, an earlier bachelor degree, or non-matriculated status. Medical exemption requires licensed-provider documentation and authorized approval with both academic and wellness offices. Transfer wellness work requires department review; varsity seasons earn wellness activity credit. Final-semester prior learning or certification may count with Wellness Education approval. Club and intramural sports do not count.

requirements.title: Degree requirements and typical sequence charts
requirements.summary: The university graduation page directs students to catalog program requirements and says programmatic writing-intensive courses are identified by WI on typical course-sequence charts. The AI chart is relevant published curricular evidence, but the unresolved Immersion 3 annotation and exact WI mapping prevent a complete audit.

notes: The catalog curriculum was read through the ordinary browser. Automated catalog access returned a JavaScript/bot-access shell; no access controls were bypassed. The adapter observes the accessible study-page identity and co-op requirement only.
The catalog calls its table a typical course sequence. This record preserves its inventory and alternatives without claiming a mandatory semester order.

Original numeric hours are preserved and normalized as semester hours using the university graduation policy. Individual alternative-course amounts remain unverified. A repeated zero-hour co-op course is one identity plus a two-block rule.
Fall 2026 admission availability is not treated as evidence of actual first instruction. Activity and first-offered date remain unknown.
The MATH-190 row has an Immersion 3 annotation while a separate fourth-year Immersion 3 slot appears. No double-counting or waiver is inferred.

Public undergraduate policies D02.0/D05.0/D12.0 now cover transfer, grading/repeats, GPA, residency and degree minimums. The university semester-credit basis is explicit. Degree completeness remains partial for writing/general-education/college scope and the catalog sequence conflict; no graduate policy is inherited.

2026-10-11: General education and wellness policies reviewed; approved-course directory retrieval stopped at unavailable robots response (202) after the public registrar redirect. No automated catalog access was inferred.

The launch article is dated March 25 and explicitly updated August 17, 2026; its Fall 2026 first-cohort statement supports a planned term, not confirmed first instruction. Program-aim statements are not measured graduate outcomes.
